Go 1.26.6 is the current security-patched point release after the original 1.26.5 decision; language and application contracts remain unchanged.

The reusable no-tabs widget aligns utility combobox, cache, retry projection, nested upload, and explicit profile-save behavior with the self-hosted gateway contract.

notes: The hierarchy is additive and does not rewrite the completed self-hosted plan or phases.

P00.S04 first green 32-sample run was not accepted because the harness grouped task p50 wall time, omitted grouped CPU, and measured Docker client CPU for browser containers; the benchmark was corrected and the unchanged task observations were deterministically re-aggregated.
A pre-reference browser smoke failed with the default container shared-memory limit; the runner now uses the pinned browser image with --shm-size 2g. No accepted sample failed.
The initial KER is measured only on the recorded Linux/Go/Node/Docker/Compose fingerprint; no synthetic DOM dependency is accepted in the initial implementation.

P01.S07 EVAL-002 passed with four CPU slots: warm p95 wall 8078 ms versus the 20495.2 ms budget, all-sample peak RSS 486.2265625 MiB versus the accepted 601.09 MiB budget, zero failures, zero leaks, and identical six-task selection across all eight samples.

P01 fixture-only RED corrections retained the intended runner assertions, including bounded timeout termination; the provisional eight-slot evaluation was rejected for raw RSS variance and was not used as accepted evidence.

P02 converted all safe deterministic frontend modules to async ownership, retained exactly the SessionVault lifecycle/clock and observability configuration exceptions, and added explicit LiveView Req allowances plus view/proxy teardown.

P02 replaced one process-global malformed-login SessionVault count assertion with request-local session absence assertions; this preserved the user-visible security oracle while making the test valid under concurrent execution.

P02's first ten-seed attempt exposed a Req ownership cleanup race at seed 181081 and was rejected; the explicit allowance/teardown boundary was added, and the final ten-seed EVAL-003 passed with zero failures/leaks at 4125 ms warm p95 versus the 10033 ms sequential frontend reference.

P03 extracted the pure client decision core into frontend/assets/js/client_core.mjs, imported it from app.js, added TEST-046/051, and kept browser effects in thin hooks with no package manifest or DOM emulator.
P03 EVAL-004 passed 30 warm client-core samples at 495 ms p95 and 120.3984375 MiB maximum RSS, with zero failures/leaks/package installs/network attempts.

P03's unqualified benchmark command accidentally selected baseline mode and started backend verification; the exact runner-owned scratch directory was cleaned, no evidence was accepted, and the command was corrected to explicit task mode with zero cold samples.

P04 replaced the monolithic ordinary browser workflow with exactly two targeted canaries and kept Compose smoke separate; the pinned browser image uses host networking, the Docker socket, and 2 GiB shared memory.
P04 browser coverage found the real SecretStager api-key serialization mismatch; the production handler now accepts the hyphenated public-event key while preserving write-only credential behavior.

P04 EVAL-005 passed five warm browser samples at 39621 ms p95 and 403.08203125 MiB maximum RSS, with two ordinary browser features per sample, zero failures/leaks/screenshots/running containers, and unchanged P00 budgets.

P04's initial browser benchmark invocation was made explicit with task mode and zero cold samples; browser-specific comparison now checks feature inventory, session count, screenshots, and cleanup. Browser task CPU remains informational because the Docker-client measurement is not equivalent to Chromium-process CPU.

P06 EVAL-007 passed one complete release candidate with all 25 selected tasks green, zero failures, zero leaked resources, and two ordinary service-pool starts. The release critical path was 233358 ms and peak RSS was 1165.16796875 MiB; these are release-graph observations rather than new tier budgets. The release candidate was measured with the pinned Elixir/OTP PATH required by the reference host.

P06 failed attempts were not accepted as evidence: the first release invocation used an incomplete lifecycle status, the next omitted the pinned Elixir/OTP PATH, and the initial Compose certification required causal fixes for browser-image pinning, login-shell PATH rewriting, host-path Docker mounts, and the fake-provider Responses inference type. No test oracle, assertion purpose, or resource threshold was weakened; failed-attempt scratch artifacts were removed.

P07 found and corrected a real deployed-launcher defect: the pinned browser image contains Chromium and the toolchain but not frontend Hex dependencies, so the launcher now performs the same Hex/Rebar/deps bootstrap as the canonical browser tier.

P07 found and corrected a real deployed-canary timing/state defect: persisted LiveView fold state and asynchronous UI-state saves could disable the next fold. TEST-056 now waits for enabled controls, opens only when collapsed, and asserts the visible body without changing the oracle.
P07 deployment identity intentionally distinguishes application-bearing release 761f5f76 from later test/docs-only merges 23538c2 and 40083fd; no later application image input changed.

P07 initial deployment used an unsafe shell source for JSON environment values and produced a healthy-configuration failure; recovery used Compose --env-file, preserved named volumes, and passed health, public probes, and TEST-056.
P07 cleanup removed root-owned browser scratch artifacts and the exact exited stale otel-collector-state-init-1 orphan; no task-owned test container or volume remained.
